text.p: European aircraft consortium Airbus said on Monday that Singapore Airlines regional carrier unit SilkAir had made firm orders for three A319 aircraft and five A320s and had options for 10 more planes.
Airbus said in a statement SilkAir planned to buy up to 18 new generation aircraft from the A320 product line.
"This package covers firm orders for three 124-seat A319s and five 150-seat A320s, plus options for a further 10 aircraft of any type from the family," it said.
"In addition to the A319 and A320, this also includes the 185-seat A321, which would be able to meet the airline's future growth requirements at the upper end of the regional market." it said.
The aircraft on firm order were replacing the B373 fleet and were for delivery starting September 1998, it said. No value was given for the deal.

Airbus Industrie is a consortium made up of French state-owned Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.
